# Compact Fusion Reactor
The station runs on a compact fusion reactor. The reactor itself makes no electricity: it heats coolant gas, and a [color=orange]gas turbine[/color] turns that heat into power for the [color=orange]HV network[/color].
## The loop 1. Coolant gas is pumped into the reactor [color=lightblue]inlet[/color]. Examine the reactor to see which side it is on. 2. The gas passes the core, heats up and leaves through the [color=orange]outlet[/color]. 3. Hot gas goes into the turbine inlet. The turbine takes heat from it and makes power. 4. Gas leaving the turbine is still warm. Vent it, or cool it in radiators and send it back to the reactor.
The hotter and denser the gas entering the turbine, the more power it makes. About half of the heat above room temperature is taken out, so the exhaust is still hot.
A good cold loop matters: the colder the gas entering the reactor, the more heat it can carry away, and the higher you can run the reactor before the core overheats. Denser coolant (higher pressure) carries more heat too.
## Running the reactor - The containment field needs [color=orange]APC power[/color]. Without it the reactor winds down and the field weakens. - Insert a [color=cyan]fuel cassette[/color]. Cassettes are ordered from cargo. The cassette is locked in while the reactor runs. - Set the power and press [bold]Start reactor[/bold]. Output rises gradually. - Higher power burns fuel faster and heats the core faster. The core only stays cool if enough gas flows through it.
## Danger Above the safe core temperature the containment field starts to fail; the hotter the core, the faster it fails. Engineering is warned over the radio as the field weakens.
If the field reaches 0%, the reactor [color=red]breaches[/color]: an explosion, a burst of superheated gas, and an electromagnetic pulse that knocks out nearby electronics. The reactor is wrecked.
[bold]Shutting down always works.[/bold] Press Shut down, keep coolant flowing, and the core cools on its own.
## Turbine Gas hotter than the turbine can take wears down its blades. A turbine with wrecked blades makes no power until it is repaired with a [color=orange]welder[/color].
